prerequisites: Prior knowledge of digital signal processing
Solid foundation in algebra and statistics

learning_outcomes.text: Possess and understand knowledge that provides a basis or opportunity to be original in the development and/or application of ideas, often in a research context
Students should be able to apply acquired knowledge and problem-solving skills in new or unfamiliar environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way
Students should possess learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way
Ability to project, calculate and design products, processes and installations in all areas of telecommunication engineering.

Ability for mathematical modeling, calculation and simulation in technology and engineering company centers, particularly in research, development and innovation tasks in all areas related to Telecommunication Engineering and related multidisciplinary fields.
Ability to apply acquired knowledge and solve problems in new or unfamiliar environments within broader and multidisciplinary contexts, being able to integrate knowledge.
Ability to communicate (orally and in writing) conclusions - and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them - to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Possess skills for continuous, self-directed and autonomous learning.
Ability to apply methods of information theory, adaptive modulation and channel coding, as well as advanced digital signal processing techniques to communication and audiovisual systems.
Ability to develop radiocommunication systems: antenna design, equipment and subsystems, channel modeling, link calculation and planning.
Ability to implement wired, line, satellite systems in fixed and mobile communication environments.
Apply digital signal processing techniques for the development and implementation of communication, audiovisual and multimedia systems.
Apply information theory techniques for the development and implementation of communication and audiovisual systems.

Know and apply methods for characterizing and modeling the communication channel, and apply, design and develop different techniques for adapting to it, including channel coding and adaptive modulation techniques.

Know and apply methods for characterizing and modeling the communication channel, and apply, design and develop different techniques for correcting the distortion introduced by it, including channel equalization techniques.

Design communication subsystems based totally or partially on digital signal processing techniques, as well as implement these subsystems in fixed and mobile communication environments, using the most appropriate technology.
Design systems based on spatial diversity to increase communication efficiency and channel adaptation capability.

syllabus_topics: Advanced digital signal processing techniques and information theory for channel characterization in communication, audiovisual and multimedia systems.
Adaptation and correction of the communication channel in varying environments.
Communication systems based on digital signal processing techniques and spatial diversity.
Implementation of adaptive systems and subsystems.

assessment_methods.method: Final exam on problems and questions related to course content

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final exam accounts for 70%, the lab work for 20%, and the group presentation for 10%. To pass, both the written exam and the work must score at least 4 out of 10, and the final combined grade (0.7 * exam grade + 0.2 * work grade + 0.1 * presentation grade) must be at least 5 points. For the extraordinary call, the final exam accounts for 70% and a practical exam accounts for 30%. Students who completed the practical work and presentation in the ordinary call may keep their grades for these components instead of taking the practical exam. To pass, both the theory and practical parts of the evaluation must score at least 4 out of 10, and the final combined grade must be at least 5 points.
